newsitem.title: GERMANY: Munich Re's ERGO sees Europe acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Munich Re's ERGO sees Europe acquisitions.

text.p: The designated head of the planned new German insurer ERGO Versicherungsgruppe said on Monday the group will want to expand its operations in Europe through acquisitions.
Reinsurance group Munich Re on Thursday announced that ERGO, a holding company in which it will have a majority stake, would be created by the fusion of Victoria Holding AG and Hamburg-Mannheimer AG.

Edgar Jannott, the chairman of Victoria who is set to lead the ERGO group if the German cartel office approves the merger, said only 1.5 billion marks ($858.4 million) of the group's combined 21 billion marks premium income came from foreign business.

"This relationship is unbalanced. ERGO wants to buy life and specialist insurers on the European market," Jannott told reporters, adding that ERGO was not seeking to expand outside of Europe at the moment.
Jannott did not specify which firms ERGO was interested in, but said Munich Re would carry the financial burden of ERGO's expansion plan.
Jannot said he was happy with the deal to link up with Hamburg-Mannheimer AG and said it meant Munich Re had stopped more of the German market being acquired by foreign firms.
Munich Re owns 80 percent of Hamburg-Mannheimer and has an 18 percent direct stake in Victoria as well as an indirect holding of 5.3 percent.

The inclusion of Victoria within Munich Re will boost the latter's consolidated premium by some 8.4 billion marks to about 46.6 billion marks, making it the country's second largest insurer after Allianz AG. ($ = 1.747 German Marks)
